findings.summary: crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: The CHANGELOG rule skips every limit that names no file, including forms that contradict the forced CHANGELOG.md edit, so part of the class stays open.
findings.evidence: ensure_changelog (reading.rs:297-319) adds CHANGELOG.md to every change reading unconditionally. limits_changed_files (briefs.rs:140-146) recognises 'test-only change' and 'only X may change' with X a non-file word ('only the docs may change'). A reading with the criterion 'test-only change' would still produce a CHANGELOG.md edit that its own limit text forbids, which is the 9bw7 shape. The plan accepts it because the text names no file. The accepted reading's design applies the rule to every scope limit; this narrowing is not raised as a departure for these forms. Fix: Apply the CHANGELOG half to every criterion for which limits_changed_files is true. Exempt only limits that point at the deliverables (contain 'deliverable'), the bare 'no other file changed' form with no exception list, or text naming CHANGELOG.md. Add a corpus Refuse case and a unit assertion for 'test-only change' and 'only the docs may change', and keep 'no other file changed' as Accept.
findings.location: Decision 2 / Step 2 (`names_a_file` gate on the CHANGELOG half)

findings.summary: The consumer rule can be met without widening the allowlist, so the 7z81 failure still reaches verification.
findings.evidence: allowed_paths (briefs.rs:110-126) makes the deliverable list the allowlist whenever a criterion limits files. Under the plan, 'Consumers: crates/athena-cli/tests/common/mod.rs loads athena.toml' satisfies the rule even if that file is not a deliverable. The producer then has to edit it, and the scope guard fails the job exactly as in 20261018-045437-7z81. Any unrelated crates/ test deliverable (for example refusal_corpus.rs) also satisfies it. The 7z81 introspection's prevention was that the reading should then allow those files. The plan names this weakness only as a risk ('cannot verify the search'). Fix: Require every crates/ path named in a `Consumers:` line to be a deliverable, unless the same line says the file needs no change (for example the word 'unchanged'). Also accept a `Consumers:` line that says the search found none, so a reader can state that result. Drop or tighten the 'any crates/ test deliverable' shortcut so it does not stand in for the search. Add unit and corpus cases: a `Consumers:` line naming a non-deliverable path is refused, and the same path as a deliverable is accepted.
findings.location: Decision 3 / Step 2 (consumer half: `Consumers:` line or any crates/ test deliverable)

findings.summary: The plan hard-codes CHANGELOG.md a second time instead of reusing the constant ensure_changelog uses.
findings.evidence: reading.rs:293 defines `const CHANGELOG_PATH: &str = "CHANGELOG.md";`, the path ensure_changelog forces. checks.rs is a child module of reading, so it can use `super::CHANGELOG_PATH`. A separate literal in a new table can drift from what is actually written. Fix: Build the DEFAULT_WRITTEN_FILES row from `super::CHANGELOG_PATH` (or move the constant into the table and have ensure_changelog read it), so the gate and the writer share one source.

findings.summary: The plan says its test shows both the literal and the production form of criterion 2, but the literal form (CHANGELOG.md as a deliverable, limit text silent) is refused, not accepted.
findings.evidence: Criterion 2 says the same reading 'with CHANGELOG.md listed is accepted'. The demonstration asserts that a reading with CHANGELOG.md as a deliverable but omitted from the limit is still refused, and accepts only the reading whose limit names CHANGELOG.md. The reading's design allows listing CHANGELOG.md 'as a deliverable ... or name it in the limit', so the plan's acceptance matches one of the two allowed forms, but the wording overstates what is shown. Fix: State in the demonstration that 'listed' is taken as named in the limit text (the reading's second allowed form), and drop the claim that the literal deliverable-only form is shown as accepted. Keep the open question for the user.

summary: The plan's references check out. `limits_changed_files` (briefs.rs:146) and `refusing_check` (checks.rs:515) exist; the new step after `check_defined_terms` (checks.rs:540) keeps the step-order tests at reading.rs:4713, 5196, 7219 and 7918 passing; and `ensure_changelog` (reading.rs:297) runs before the gate (build_reading at reading.rs:859, gate at reading.rs:680), so decision 1 is sound. The only fixture that pushes a limit through the real gate is LIMIT at run/tests.rs:3213, and the plan handles it. run_pin_tests.rs:1396 calls the send-back text directly, not the gate. D166 is the next free decision id. Each demonstration has a fails-without case and uses real entry points with no double. Two soundness gaps would each let one of the two cited jobs' failures recur. (1) The CHANGELOG half fires only when the limit text names a file, so limits like 'test-only change' or 'only the docs may change', which conflict just as much with the forced CHANGELOG.md edit, pass the gate. (2) The consumer half accepts a `Consumers:` line naming any crates/ path, or any crates/ test deliverable, without the named consumers becoming deliverables. Since the deliverable list is the allowlist at verification, job 7z81's scope-guard failure can still happen after the gate accepts the reading. Both have simple, more correct alternatives, so the verdict is revise.
